name: 6-APDB
addictionPotential: Moderately addictive with a high potential for abuse
toxicities: Toxicity and long-term health effects of recreational 6-APDB appear not to have been studied and exact toxic dose is unknown because its human-use history is short.
effectsSummary: 6-APDB as a benzofuran empathogen related to 6-APB and reports empathogenic, stimulant and mild psychedelic effects; its effects index is based on anecdotal reports.
dosageRemark: The archived oral dose table lists threshold 20 mg, light 30-70 mg, moderate 70-100 mg, strong 100-130 mg and heavy 130 mg+; total duration 6-8 h, onset and comeup 30-60 min, peak 2-3 h and offset 2-3 h. Educational user/resource compilation, not a recommendation. The model does not represent the threshold separately, so 20 mg is preserved here and lightMin follows the source light range lower bound.
generalRisks: Recreational toxicity and long-term health effects appear unstudied and the exact dose that causes poisoning is unknown; it advises starting lower because of individual differences in weight, tolerance, metabolism and sensitivity.
longtermRisks: Long-term health effects of recreational 6-APDB appear not to have been studied.
saferUse: FreeODwiki advises starting lower due to differences in weight, tolerance, metabolism and individual sensitivity.
It recommends independent research and harm reduction because toxicity and long-term effects are poorly characterized.
summary: A stimulant and entactogen related to MDMA and an analogue of MDA. Reported as being fairly psychedlic at higher doses. It is a triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor. Potent full agonist of serotonin 2B receptors.
